nodes.reason: מצוה (commandment) is essentially a unit of sacred obligation — its nature belongs to the domain of holiness and divine service. The Torah teaches that each mitzvah draws the next, establishing mitzvah as the fundamental building block of the righteous path.

בין המצוות (the dimension between the mitzvot) is the sacred space that connects one commandment to the next. Its essential nature is a holy dimension (בְּחִינָה שֶׁל קְדֻשָּׁה) — the Rebbe explicitly calls it 'יְקָרָה מְאֹד' (very precious). It belongs with מצוה in the same domain of holiness and divine service, as it is the connective tissue of the mitzvot.

new_packages.rationale: No bechina-based packages exist for this Torah. Both nodes — מצוה and בין המצוות — belong to the domain of holiness and sacred service. They form a natural thematic cluster: the commandment itself and the precious sacred dimension between commandments. The Torah's entire argument revolves around these two concepts and how they interact causally (the mitzvah draws the next via the in-between dimension), but their essential nature is unified in the domain of קדושה.
